I forgot it was a broken link, but looks like you found it
Yes—the note moved into Investigation 12’s brainstorm folder. I found the relocation record and current register, including Note 07, so I’m continuing from that work.

A promising finite result has emerged: local polynomial factors let us control the current through collisions without a lower bound on \(H_z\). I’m checking whether this proves convergence as the smoothing parameter vanishes, as well as a finite bound. The remaining issue is whether theta-specific estimates can make that bound useful at high height.

The proof now gives a coarse bound from the complete theta source itself: positivity at one anchor point, together with source moment bounds, controls the regularized current. It allows crossings and needs no \(H_z\) floor. The bound may be very large, so it does not yet justify a larger backward width or a simplicity conclusion.

The internal review supports both results: the regularized current converges to the actual smooth positive flux, and the anchor estimate gives a finite bound from the complete source. I’m saving the proof and review and updating OBF-02/03. Useful high-height bounds and the earlier nonreal population remain open.

Continued from Note 07 and saved [Note 08: Anchored small-value bounds and the exact current limit](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/12_height_dependent_heat_contours/brainstorm/notes/08_ANCHORED_SMALL_VALUES_AND_EXACT_CURRENT_LIMIT_20261023.md).

The new work:

- Proves convergence of the regularized current to the actual smooth positive flux, including through collisions.
- Derives a coarse finite negative-time theta bound from a positive anchor and complete source moments, without an \(H_z\) floor.
- Improves the local near-real strip error from \(O(\delta)\) to \(O(\delta^2)\) for symmetric windows.

The proof uses [Parusiński–Rainer’s polynomial-root theorem](https://math.univ-cotedazur.fr/~parus/publis/ens.pdf). I saved a [same-model internal review](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/12_height_dependent_heat_contours/brainstorm/reviews/03_ANCHORED_SMALL_VALUES_AND_CURRENT_LIMIT_REVIEW_20261023.md) and updated the [OBF progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/12_height_dependent_heat_contours/brainstorm/research-progress/01_OPEN_BOUNDARY_FLUX_PROGRESS_20261023.md).

**The remaining gap is useful size:** the bound may be enormous at high height. No improved backward width or simplicity conclusion follows yet, and the earlier nonreal population remains separately unbounded.

Can you include all of this in the manuscript. Try to focus on analytic results, and on elegance of the results. I believe these results are starting to become quite elegant, so we want to focus on that. In fact, it might be worth making a new version that is meant to be the proof "from the book" in the sense of Erdos. So we can think of the current manuscript as the first draft for the one from the book. So only write results into that draft if you think they belong there.

I’ll read the current manuscript and shape a new, more selective version around the strongest analytic results. I’ll keep the proofs precise and leave acquisition details and weaker estimates in the research notes where they would interrupt the exposition.
I’m treating the new version as a concise mathematical paper, with complete proofs and a clear central argument. I’ll use the PDF skill to compile and inspect the reading copy.
For that paper, I want to focus on the most elegant formula characterizing these results, with a flux term, and a natural boundary (presumably flowing with the heat flow)
For me that seems like the most elegant result here, it should center on that

That gives the paper a clearer center. I’ll build it around conservation of nonreal zeros in a moving region: the change in population equals inward flux relative to the boundary, less the loss at real collisions. I’ll check which boundary motions make that formula natural, and what happens if the boundary follows the zero motion exactly.
Yes and on trying to estimate those terms as effectively as possible using actual information from \theta / \xi

I’ll make the theta/xi input part of the central argument. In particular, I’ll look for a heat-adapted boundary whose relative flux can be bounded by a coupled expression from the complete field, so the paper shows both the conservation law and what information actually controls its terms.
\theta or \xi that is, arithmetic information I mean

Understood—arithmetic information specific to theta or xi, beyond positivity, decay, and generic heat-flow bounds. I’ll distinguish the terms we can estimate from that arithmetic from those still controlled only by general analysis, and keep any missing arithmetic estimate explicit.
The proof "from the book" should ideally characterize all of it as optimally as possible given the constraints of elegance

There is a clean centerpiece: when the boundary is defined by a reference heat field \(G\), the relative flux is governed by
\[
H_{zz}G_z-H_zG_{zz}.
\]
The boundary-velocity denominator cancels. For a reference built from the actual theta coefficients, this becomes an explicit integral coupling the retained source terms with the complete tail. I’ll center the paper on that identity, the sharp multiplicity bound, and estimates that preserve this cancellation.

The draft now centers on the exact moving-boundary balance and its cancellation formula. The first checks support a useful arithmetic refinement: the theta head–tail formula preserves cancellation lost by separate absolute moment bounds. I’m checking the full argument and keeping the distinction clear between sharp identities and estimates whose size at large height remains open.

The natural boundary now has a precise form: level curves of a reference heat field. Their motion cancels inside the flux formula, including the apparent derivative denominator. I’ve moved this result and the theta/xi estimates ahead of the technical justification, so they lead the paper.

A further refinement is worth including: the theta tail-to-head ratio is strictly decreasing. This lets us subtract the two source orderings before taking absolute values, giving a strictly sharper bound and quadratic cancellation along the diagonal. The proof is short. It also makes clear that this ordering alone does not give the flux a sign.

The mathematical checks are complete. I’m saving the selective manuscript and its review, using the write-page skill’s editorial checks within the repository’s existing format. The review records the sharp constants and the improved arithmetic bound; the remaining open task is to make the full nonreal population and flux budget small enough at large height.

The 12-page manuscript is saved, and all pages have passed the layout check. Both compilers succeeded with no warnings or missing references. The original research draft is preserved, and the progress register now records the moving-boundary result and arithmetic improvement.

Created a new 12-page [analytic manuscript](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-4/12_height_dependent_heat_contours/manuscript/book.tex), centered on the moving-boundary balance and
\[
\mathcal W(H,G)=H_{zz}G_z-H_zG_{zz}.
\]

It includes sharp multiplicity bounds and a stronger ordered theta head–tail estimate with quadratic diagonal cancellation. Useful high-height estimates remain open.
